reason: CONFIRMED on the mechanism, and it is a round-9 regression. `git log -S"b-editGroup" render-b.js` shows commit 7452ad9d (round 9) replacing `h("div", { style: "display:grid;gap:6px;line-height:1.5" }, ...)` with `h("div.b-editGroup", {}, ...)` and never adding the rule: grep .b-editGroup returns 0 hits in b.css, shell.css, fonts.css and master.html, and exactly 1 hit in render-b.js:1012. So the group computes display:block with an inline span.b-label (computed display:inline) beside an inline-flex div.b-seg, and h() emits no whitespace node between them. Driven in chromium on ?v=paper and ?v=ink at 320/360/390/768/1023/1152/1280/1440, editor open on owner-flight, the numbers are identical on both grounds at every width >= 360: label box right == .b-seg box left (154.41 at 390; 328.41 at 1440), i.e. a box-to-box gap of exactly 0.00px. Because the span is inline, its box IS its ink box, so the last glyph of SEE sits 1.76px (the trailing letter-space of --track-label) from the seg's hairline and 2.76px from the black fill of the pressed Shown pill. Cropped at 390 on both grounds the E is visibly welded to the plate. The other two groups measure a clean 6.00px label-to-input gap at every width. Not covered by either gate: interaction-check.mjs has no assertion on .b-editGroup or on this spacing (its .b-seg tests are aria-pressed, guest visibility, hit target and plate width), and audit.mjs's space-ladder check reads only the stylesheets named in build.mjs's CSS array - render-b.js's inline 6px is invisible to it, which is why the drift survived. Nothing in SETTLED.md touches it. Two claims in the framings are wrong but neither carries the finding: (a) 'the one pair whose spacing is on none of the nine declared steps' overstates - the two sibling groups' 6px is off-ladder too, just hidden from the gate in a JS inline style; (b) the ui framing's rhythm complaint ('the only label not on its own line') is not answered by its own fix, which keeps the pair on one line. The evidence framing's fix is the weaker of the two: `gap: var(--gap-hair)` lands 4px against the siblings' 6px, so it does not 'match the two groups above it', and measured it costs 19.4px of panel height (537.58 -> 556.97) and 11px of extra scroll on a 390x667 phone where the sheet already scrolls 58px. The ui framing's fix is exact and free.
sharpenedFix: Take the ui form, verbatim, as one rule in b.css beside .b-editActs (b.css:838, master.html:1221): `.b-editGroup { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--gap-control); flex-wrap: wrap; }`. --gap-control resolves to --gap-snug = 12px (shell.css:107, :94), a declared step, and the value carries no px literal so audit.mjs's source space-ladder check stays clean. Injected and measured on paper and ink at 320/360/390/768/1023/1152/1280/1440: the gap becomes exactly 12.00px at every width >= 360; the row stays 39px; .b-edit's height (537.58), top, .b-editActs top and .b-editDanger top are byte-identical to the base at every width; the sheet gains zero scroll on a 390x667 phone; at 320 it wraps to two lines with a 12px row gap, +1.89px of panel. Do NOT use the sibling framing's grid/--gap-hair variant. If the founder would rather the three groups read as one stacked pattern, that is a separate, larger change and should be done properly rather than half: drop the two inline style="display:grid;gap:6px;line-height:1.5" attributes (render-b.js:950, :976), put .b-editGroup on all three, and give the class `display: grid; gap: var(--gap-hair); justify-items: start;`. Measured, that yields 4.00px on all three, keeps line-height at 1.5 (the inline declaration was redundant - .b-edit already sets --lead-body), costs 11.4px of panel height, and moves the last off-ladder spacing in the editor out of JS and into the file the gate reads. Gate either shape with `.b-seg.getBoundingClientRect().left - .b-label.getBoundingClientRect().right === 12` (row form) or `top - bottom === 4` (stacked form), asserted with the editor open on both ?v=paper and ?v=ink.
